text: Cairn treats a dull Thursday as proof he picked wrong.
If the pile feels like homework, the passion must be fake.
So the hand goes to the lid.
The friend gets a message.
It was not the one.
That is the trap.
A hard night is not a verdict.
Find your passion is a fixed theory of interest.
It makes Cairn loyal until the spark dies.
Then it makes him leave.
The loyalty looks like love on Tuesday.
It looks like a courtroom on Thursday.
The pile did not change species overnight.
The theory did.
He does not ask what the pile needs.
He asks whether he is still the kind of person who loves this.
That question is the trap talking.
It turns a heavy paragraph into a personality test.
It turns a mismatch into a broken compass.
Cairn names it.
Then he sits back down.
The folder stays on the desk.
The chair stays pulled in.
He does not owe the night a new identity.
He owes the pile the hour he already started.
The friend can wait.
The lid can wait.
The session cannot.
A find theory treats interest like a coin under a bench.
You either found it or you did not.
When the page mismatches, the coin was fake, so you stand up and hunt another coin.
A develop theory treats interest like a muscle.
Mismatch is the first hour of training.
Same page.
Different theory.
Different heat.
When Cairn sits with a mismatching article, a find theory cools him.
A develop theory keeps him curious.
He does not need a new passion.
He needs another pass.
He does not open a new folder to feel Tuesday again.
He gives this folder a second hour before he gives it a funeral.
Taste is not a locked door.
A page can be wrong for his taste and still be worth a pass.
Develop it means stay long enough for the interest to thicken.
Cairn talks to himself like the grow group.
Not like a man who misplaced his soulmate.
